papers.title: Mega-ASR: Towards In-the-wild^2 Speech Recognition via Scaling up Real-world Acoustic Simulation
papers.abstract: Despite rapid advances in automatic speech recognition (ASR) and large audio-language models, robust recognition in real-world environments remains limited by an "acoustic robustness bottleneck": models often lose acoustic grounding and produce omissions or hallucinations under severe, compositional distortions. We propose Mega-ASR, a unified ASR-in-the-wild framework.

papers.title: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have driven growing interest in GUI agents. We propose Video2GUI, a fully automated framework that extracts grounded GUI interaction trajectories directly from unlabeled Internet videos, constructing WildGUI with 12 million interaction trajectories.

papers.title: Enhancing Train-Free Infinite-Frame Generation for Consistent Long Videos
papers.abstract: We propose MIGA, a novel infinite-frame long video generation method with a two-stage alignment mechanism and dual consistency enhancement mechanism for train-free consistent long video generation.

papers.title: You Only Need Minimal RLVR Training: Extrapolating LLMs via Rank-1 Trajectories
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that RLVR weight trajectories are extremely low-rank and highly predictable. We propose RELEX (REinforcement Learning EXtrapolation), requiring as few as 15% steps of full RLVR training while matching or exceeding performance.

papers.title: A Survey of Large Audio Language Models: Generalization, Trustworthiness, and Outlook
papers.abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive investigation into LALMs, detailing architectural innovations and alignment algorithms, while establishing a taxonomy of trustworthiness covering hallucination, robustness, safety, privacy, fairness, and authentication.

papers.title: Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era
papers.abstract: We show that time series foundation models scale: a single training recipe produces reliable forecast-quality improvements from 4M to 2.5B parameters. Toto 2.0 sets a new state of the art on three forecasting benchmarks.

papers.title: Mix-Quant: Quantized Prefilling, Precise Decoding for Agentic LLMs
papers.abstract: We propose Mix-Quant, a phase-aware quantization framework applying NVFP4 to prefilling while preserving BF16 for decoding, achieving up to 3x speedup during prefilling while largely preserving task performance.

papers.title: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
papers.abstract: We introduce CutVerse, a benchmark evaluating GUI agents in media post-production, covering 186 complex tasks across 7 professional applications. Current agents achieve only 36.0% task success rate.

papers.title: LLMEval-Logic: A Solver-Verified Chinese Benchmark for Logical Reasoning of LLMs with Adversarial Hardening
papers.abstract: We present LLMEval-Logic, a Chinese logical reasoning benchmark with Z3-verified answers. The best frontier LLM reaches only 37.5% Hard Item Accuracy, revealing substantial gaps in current models.

papers.title: SaaSBench: Exploring the Boundaries of Coding Agents in Long-Horizon Enterprise SaaS Engineering
papers.abstract: SaaSBench is the first benchmark for AI agents in enterprise SaaS engineering, spanning 30 tasks across 6 domains. Over 95% of task failures occur before agents reach deep business logic.
